chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, raising it, said:
I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) praying with a group, and he was by a corner in his house, near the wall, and all of them were on his right, and there was no one on his left.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ: Praying with a group (leading the congregation)

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam arrange the congregation when praying in a corner with limited space?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) flexibility in prayer arrangements, demonstrating that strict symmetry is not obligatory when space is constrained. It serves as a practical precedent for the Shia jurisprudential ruling that an Imam may stand to the side of the congregation or even alone, provided the prayer remains valid, reflecting the ease (*rukhas*) emphasized in Shia fiqh. This visual evidence supports the broader principle that the validity of congregational prayer depends on the intention and direction of prayer rather than rigid geometric alignment.
